Irlyava Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Irliava, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century, this cemetery existed by 1875 per epigraphic data, presumably used until WWII, though its most recent surviving gravestone dates to 1927. Jews are believed to have arrived in the late 18th century; population reached 85 by 1880 and 89 by 1910, falling to 83 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period) before recovering to 95 by 1930. Some Jews worked in agriculture and commerce. Hungarian forces arrived March 1939, persecuting Jews and forcing them from their occupations; from 1940-1941, area Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. Families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled in 1941 to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered; that same year, about 110 Jews lived in Irliava, deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
